title.narrative: Emergency Unconditional Cash Transfer (UCT) Assistance to Drought-Affected Vulnerable Households in Tayeeglow District, Bakool Region.

description.narrative: ltpgtTayeeglow District, located in the Bakool region of southwestern Somalia, includes a main town centre divided into the Sinai, Halgan, and Bolowka sections, as well as 14 surrounding villages. The district has an estimated population of 171,691, with a nearly equal gender distribution: 86,278 females (50.3%) and 85,413 males (49.7%). This area is strategically vital to agriculture and regional security and is located at 4.03°N, 44.52°E. The population is severely affected by persistent drought, with 77% of the 41,700 individuals classified as People in Need (PiN) residing in rural areas. Currently, Tayeeglow District is facing a profound humanitarian emergency, driven by the catastrophic failure of the 2025 Deyr seasonal rains, compounded by a long-term humanitarian vacuum and acute economic instability. Tragically, there is currently little to no coverage of food humanitarian aid in the area, leaving the population entirely reliant on themselves amid a collapsing economy.ltbrgtAccording to the December 2025 FSNAU/FEWSNET technical release, the Bakool region has experienced a drastic decline in food security, with 123,020 people now classified in IPC Phases 3 (Crisis) and 4 (Emergency). Within Tayeeglow District alone, approximately 11,865 households fall into these critical categories and urgently require life-saving intervention. Furthermore, an additional 208,190 people remain in IPC Phase 2, making them highly vulnerable and at risk of progressing to higher IPC phases due to resource-based conflict that could cause displacement at any time, climate shocks such as droughts, and the persistent absence of humanitarian services, worsened by Al-Shabaab's strict rules on access to free goods.ltbrgtThe situation for pastoralists has become unsustainable, as resource-based drought has decimated livelihoods and forced large-scale displacement to urban centres. Households are currently trapped in a cycle of distress coping, relying heavily on credit-based food purchases, migrating in search of manual labour, and relying on dwindling social support networks, such as kinship gifts and in-kind food. Recent field assessments by CeRID confirm a near-total collapse in local purchasing power. On average, households spend 82% of their total income on food. Yet, they are unable to meet the minimum survival threshold of 2,100 kcal per person per day or the standard Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB). This food insecurity is characterised by high Coping Strategy Index (CSI) scores and low Food Consumption Scores (FCS), primarily driven by significant livestock mortality and rising debt levels that have eroded households' resilience.ltbrgtTo prevent a further humanitarian disaster, CeRID proposes a targeted, life-saving intervention to restore food access for 2,905 of the most food-insecure households in Tayeelow/Sinai, Koorar, El-Garas and Shimo village(approximately 17,430 individuals), enabling them to receive monthly (UCT) for three rounds. This effort primarily focuses on informal drought-displaced persons in Tayeeglow town and destitute pastoralists, with special emphasis on female-headed households, pregnant and lactating women, child-headed households, persons with disabilities (PWD), and the elderly.ltbrgtThe proposed transfer value, aligned with the FSNAU post-Gu assessment, the HCT-endorsed JIAF methodology, and the proposal guidelines, is USD 55 per household per month. This amount represents 70% of the Food MEB (USD $79). It provides the critical buffer needed to prevent mortality and stabilise poor and middle-class households that are currently falling through the cracks of the existing humanitarian response. Despite the severity of the crisis, existing partners are unable to reach these vulnerable populations due to significant funding constraints and access barriers. CeRID's established presence and operational capacity in Tayeeglow position the organisation to fill this vital gap and provide immediate relief to those in hard-to-reach pastoral villages.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtlt/pgt
